use_when: Naming the layer above a section head — the small marked label that makes a page read as a design file rather than a brochure.
dont_use_when: As the heading itself: it is a `<span>` and carries no heading semantics, so screen-reader users navigating by heading will not find it — put a real `<h2>` underneath. As a status on a thing: use Chip. Anywhere it needs to be clicked.
placement: Directly above a section heading, at the top of a page section or a card.
a11y: The mark is a decorative character and is aria-hidden, so a screen reader reads the title rather than announcing 'white diamond'. Title and label are ordinary text — selectable, scalable, and read in visual order. It carries no heading role and no landmark: it labels the heading that follows and does not replace it. All four tones fall below 4.5:1 in day mode; that is measured, ruled on, and recorded in decisions.md. The mark also renders narrower than its Figma node because Instrument Sans has no glyph for it — a design gap raised in Eyebrow.css, not a layout bug.
